She talks with a guest about whatever is weighing on them, and when a reading would help she picks a tradition (I Ching, Zi Wei Dou Shu, tarot, a few others) and the guest draws the cast. She is openly an AI. There's a daily free allowance, and past it, talking with her costs credits. Every change to her goes through a written proposal that says what was wrong, usually with numbers from production. articles.title: Link Building in 2027: Why Earned Authority Matters More Than Volume
articles.excerpt: The next phase of link building may look less like a production line and more like a newsroom. In a guide to link building in 2027, Search Engine Land contributor Nicole Franco argues that sustainable…
articles.body: The next phase of link building may look less like a production line and more like a newsroom. In a guide to link building in 2027, Search Engine Land contributor Nicole Franco argues that sustainable visibility will depend on earned authority: original stories, useful source material, credible journalist relationships and editorial mentions that people may genuinely discover and trust. The argument is not that links have ceased to matter. It is that raw link volume is a poor organizing metric when search systems, publishers and AI-powered discovery products can assess much broader signals of credibility and relevance . A placement that reaches the right audience and accurately connects a brand to a subject can have value beyond its backlink.

articles.body: Imagina que lideras un equipo de Customer Success en una empresa SaaS B2B. Tu equipo gestiona cientos de cuentas y cada semana tiene que decidir cuáles requieren atención urgente, cuáles pueden esperar y qué acción concreta tomar con cada una. El problema no es saber que una cuenta está en riesgo. Los datos ya existen: health score, adopción, NPS, tickets abiertos, días sin reunión. El problema es que convertir esos datos en un diagnóstico claro y un plan de acción consume tiempo y depende de la experiencia de cada especialista. articles.title: systemd-creds: TPM and host binding solve different theft cases
articles.excerpt: systemd-creds: TPM and host binding solve different theft cases Encrypted service credentials are often treated as a single category. On systemd systems, systemd-creds supports encryption keys derived…
articles.body: systemd-creds: TPM and host binding solve different theft cases Encrypted service credentials are often treated as a single category. On systemd systems, systemd-creds supports encryption keys derived from the local TPM2 device, a host file, or a combination. Those choices protect against different attackers. An operator who selects a mode without understanding the difference can create a credential that survives an image copy or one that fails after a legitimate upgrade. The host key is stored on the host file system, commonly under /var/lib/systemd/ . It protects a credential from casual inspection of the service unit or a backup that contains only the encrypted file. Anyone who obtains the encrypted credential and the host key can decrypt it.

articles.excerpt: Venus reaches peak brightness in the predawn sky this week, here's how to find it.
articles.body: Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
articles.excerpt: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
